definitions.gloss: character shape; letterform; glyph; form of a written character
definitions.explanation: The visual form or shape of a written character, whether kanji, kana, or alphabetic letters. Used when discussing handwriting, typography, calligraphy, or the structural components of characters.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{字形|じけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{似|に}ている→似る：01159_niru⟧。
examples.english: These kanji have similar character shapes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧{字形|じけい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{心|こころ}がけましょう→心がける：10015_kokorogakeru⟧。
examples.english: Let's try to write with correct character forms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{旧字体|きゅうじたい}→旧字体：27161_kyuujitai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{新字体|しんじたい}→新字体：27162_shinjitai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{字形|じけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧もの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are characters whose forms differ significantly between the old and new character standards.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧ ('character; letter') and {形|けい} ('shape; form'). A term used across calligraphy, typography, education, and kanji studies to discuss the visual appearance of written characters.

USAGE:
- In education, used when teaching students to write characters correctly: proper stroke order produces the right {字形|じけい}
- In typography, refers to the design of character shapes in fonts
- In kanji studies, discusses differences between ⟦{旧字体|きゅうじたい}→旧字体：27161_kyuujitai⟧ (old forms) and ⟦{新字体|しんじたい}→新字体：27162_shinjitai⟧ (simplified forms)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {字形|じけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{似|に}ている→似る：01159_niru⟧: to have a similar character shape
- {字形|じけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧: to differ in character form
- ⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧{字形|じけい}: correct character form
- {字形|じけい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{変遷|へんせん}→変遷：05571_hensen⟧: evolution of character forms

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{書体|しょたい}→書体：13024_shotai⟧: typeface; font; script style — refers to a consistent design style (e.g., ⟦{楷書|かいしょ}→楷書：13247_kaisho⟧, ⟦{行書|ぎょうしょ}→行書：19195_gyousho⟧) rather than the shape of individual characters
- ⟦{筆跡|ひっせき}→筆跡：17416_hisseki⟧: handwriting; penmanship — the characteristic style of a person's writing
- ⟦{字体|じたい}→字体：03337_jitai⟧: character form; variant form — focuses on different standard versions of the same character (old vs. new)
